title: The Power of the Gospel in Education
speaker: Pastor Tito Lyro

outline.title: The Preeminence of Christ in All Things
subpoints: Christ is the source, sustainer, and goal of all creation
Believers are translated from darkness to the kingdom of the Son
Christ’s supremacy extends to every area of life, not just salvation

outline.title: Education as a Sphere of Christ’s Lordship
subpoints: Teaching and learning are part of 'all things' subject to Christ
Rejection of functional deism in Christian living
Education must not be unequally yoked with unbelief

outline.title: The Purpose of Christian Education
subpoints: To nurture the whole person toward their proper end
To glorify God and enjoy Him forever
To enable students to think God’s thoughts after Him and act as vice-regents

outline.title: The Biblical Mandate for the Life of the Mind
subpoints: Renewing the mind to discern God’s will
Bringing every thought and way of thinking captive to Christ
Meditating on what is true, good, and praiseworthy

outline.title: Christ-Centered Knowledge
subpoints: Nothing can be known fully apart from the light of Christ
All intellectual pursuits must be done for the glory of God
Deviation from this principle is a distortion of truth

summary:
In this afternoon sermon, Pastor Tito Lyro explores the profound implications of Christ’s sovereignty for the realm of education. Grounded in Colossians 1:13-18, the message emphasizes that Jesus is not merely a savior who redeems souls for heaven, but the Lord who governs all aspects of existence. The pastor argues against a 'functional deist' view of faith, asserting that because all things were created through, by, and for Christ, every sphere of life—including teaching and learning—must acknowledge His preeminence.

The sermon defines Christian education as the nurture and development of the whole person toward their proper end: to glorify God and enjoy Him forever. Drawing on the works of theologians like D.L. Dabney and Cornelius Van Til, the message outlines the goal of education as enabling individuals to think God’s thoughts after Him and to serve as vice-regents under Christ’s rule. This perspective calls parents and educators to reject being 'unequally yoked' with secular or unbelieving frameworks in their approach to learning.

Finally, the sermon addresses the biblical mandate for the 'life of the mind.' Citing passages from Romans, 2 Corinthians, and Philippians, it highlights the necessity of renewing the mind, bringing every thought captive to Christ, and meditating on truth. The central thesis is that no subject or intellectual pursuit can be fully understood or properly executed unless it is viewed through the lens of who Jesus is and what He has accomplished, ensuring that all knowledge is ultimately directed toward the glory of God.
